newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian General News - Feb 4.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian General News - Feb 4.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

According to the Australian Electoral Commission's annual returns, big companies in Australia swung their financial support strongly back behind the Coalition in the lead-up to the 1996 federal election. And although business has traditionally supported the Coalition parties, the gap between corporate funding directed to the Coalition and the Labor Party appears to have increased even further. Page 1.

The Minerals Council of Australia, the nation's peak mining industry representative, has told Prime Minister John Howard he should validate all post-1994 mining leases which are now possibly invalid after the High Court's Wik decision and proceed with a rage of amendments to the Native Title Act. Page 2.

Following last year's ministerial code breaches, which resulted in two government resignations, a report, prepared by the Prime Minister's Department, has recommended that federal ministers facing a potential conflict of interest be given the option of putting their financial interests into blind trusts instead of divesting them. Page 3.

A Melbourne Magistrates Court has been told an art dealer who claimed he was a friend of painter Albert Tucker stole 81 artworks with an estimated value of A$3.7 million from the artist's Melbourne home during 1994. Tucker said that after confronting his former personal assistant, Max Michael Joffe, with the allegations, Joffe had returned with 30 of the works. Page 3.
THE AUSTRALIAN

The Federal parliamentary secretary for health and family services, Senator Bob Woods, a senior Liberal from New South Wales, announced his resignation last night, saying recent events, including the death of Senator John Panizza, had made him realise the high price of political life. Woods denied the move was connected with Australian Federal Police inquiries into his parliamentary expenses. Page 1.

In a move likely to trigger a backlash from environmental groups, the federal government has guaranteed the troubled timber industry's future for 20 years with the first of a series of agreements under a national forest peace plan announced in Victoria's vast Gippsland area. Page 1.

Western Queensland was declared a natural disaster area yesterday as floods in the state worsened. Six thousand homes were threatened in Charleville, the area's worst-hit town, with floodwaters from the Warrego River having already forced the evacuation of 180 residences. Page 1.

Helen Darville, who as Helen Demidenko caused an international literary furore less than two years ago for faking her identity, has been accused by Peter Anspach, the American author of an article on the Internet, of plagiarising his work for a column in Queensland's Courier Mail - the newspaper which exposed her identity. Page 1.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Under a code of conduct to be released today by New South Wales Police Commissioner Peter Ryan in an effort to ease public concerns about the force raised inside and outside the New South Wales Police Royal Commission over the past to years, the state's police will be forced to obey clear standards of behaviour or face possible sacking. Page 1.

According to Australian Electoral Commission documents which have revealed a loophole in legislation, donations worth nearly A$5.75 million have been funnelled to the Liberal Party through secretive trusts, avoiding strict disclosure laws. The 1995/96 eletoral donation returns show the Liberals' biggest single donor was the Free Enterprise Foundation, which donated A$3 million. Page 1.

A new wave of competition has swept the home loan market, with ANZ responding yesterday to a new loan with a rate of 6.99 percent from non-bank lender Finance Express by slashing the variable interest rate on its "no-frills" Money Saver loan to just 6.95 percent, the lowest rate in the market. Page 1.

The Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade, in its formal submission to the Mansfield inquiry into the ABC, warned Bob Mansfield last year that the closure of Radio Australia would harm Australia's international interests and could damage the billion-dollar export market in education services to Asia. However, Mansfield has recommended the ABC close the service and use the savings to boost broadcasting within Australia. Page 3.
THE AGE

According to donation figures made public by the Australian Electoral Commission, corporate Australia has turned its back on the Australian Labor Party. High powered groups such as the National Australia Bank, WMC, Village Roadshow and Victoria's Crown Caino made substantial contributions, bolstering Federal Liberal Party coffers by A$18.7 million. Page A1.

Conceding defeat for the weekend's state by-election loss in Gippsland, Victorian Premier Jeff Kennett has dismissed claims of unease among government MPs. However, federal Industrial Relations Minister Peter Reith has called for the Kennett government to listen to voters' concerns after the loss of one the safest Liberal country seats to a Labor-aligned Independent. Page A1.

In a major court battle involving 27 legal counsels, trustees acting for 45,000 unit-holders in the collapsed Estate Mortgage trusts claimed up to A$677 million damages in the Victorian Supreme Court for losses caused by allegedly high-risk investment pratices. Page A3.

Federal Immigration Minister Philip Ruddock has begun talks on next year's migrant intake, and says Australians have no reason to fear being swamped by Asians. He says only one in four Australians were born overseas and more than half of them have come from Europe. Page A3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
